expected_effect: Lower public val_bpb at matched steps: predeclared -0.001 to -0.003 bpb versus the same-host pinned control (trn21 1.005734 / 2071 or trn22 1.005967 / 2076), with step count within +/-1.5% of control (the change adds one elementwise scalar multiply on q per layer and no parameters). A candidate within +/-0.0005 of control is a null; a candidate worse by > +0.001 falsifies the hypothesis (attention at this model is already sharp enough or over-sharp at 0.12).
hypothesis: The pinned model applies a parameter-free RMS norm to q and k before attention (train.py Block.forward calls norm(q_in), norm(k_in), norm(v_in); norm() is a function, not a module with gains) and then dispatches to SDPA/nki_attention with the default softmax scale 1/sqrt(head_dim). With QK-norm the row norms of q and k are pinned to sqrt(d), so attention logits are hard-bounded to [-sqrt(d), +sqrt(d)] (about +/-11.3 at d=128) and the ONLY route to sharper attention is the scale constant, which the optimizer cannot touch. modded-nanogpt's QK-normed attention adopted a fixed scale of 0.12 at head_dim 128 (vs 1/sqrt(128)=0.0884, i.e. ~1.36x sharper attainable logits) as a record-improving change at similar depth/width. Attention numerics are demonstrably load-bearing in this model (the only autonomous KEEP at this commit is the attention-boundary change --bf16-sdpa-input: 1.002028/2233 vs 1.005967/2076). Raising the attention logit scale to 0.12 is a zero-parameter, zero-extra-matmul change (one scalar multiply of q, constant across steps so it cannot trigger recompilation) that should improve loss per step at unchanged step rate.

single_causal_change: One architecture/numerics constant change confined to train.py: a new module-level ATTN_LOGIT_SCALE (default 0.12; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_ATTN_LOGIT_SCALE overrides; CLI --attn-logit-scale FLOAT; a value <= 0 means 'use the backend default 1/sqrt(head_dim)', which is the bit-identical baseline path). When ATTN_LOGIT_SCALE > 0 and differs from 1/sqrt(head_dim), the attention module multiplies ONLY the final query tensor q by the Python-float constant q_premult = ATTN_LOGIT_SCALE * sqrt(head_dim) immediately before the attention backend call (after norm/rope/qk-shift, before any existing --bf16-sdpa-input cast), so softmax(q.k^T / sqrt(d)) becomes softmax(0.12 * q.k^T) for every backend. k, v, the SDPA/NKI kernels, all norms, the optimizer, schedule, data and evaluator are untouched. No other flag or default changes.
